chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Taking up the bass in Lloyd Hunter's band
summary: When Hunter's bassist left, Gus took two lessons from a German teacher in Omaha and was thrown into Lunceford's 'White Heat' with bleeding fingers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, let's go back to --why did we -- we were talking about Lloyd Hunter. How did we get -- how did you happen to remember that you had the quartet? Oh, because you sang. You said, what were you going to do? Here these guys were all drunk.
Yeah, that's right. And so he could get a drummer, that's what it was.
Oh, I see. But he couldn't get a bass.
He couldn't get a bass player.
Yeah.
So, the drummer was his old drummer, Debo Mills. Debo Mills came back in the band, see.
Yeah.
And so I said, 'Well, if you can get a drummer and you buy the bass, well, I'll try to play the bass.' So he said, 'Well, we'll get a teacher for you and teach you the notes.'
Fancy that.
How to the bass and everything,
really.
And you had to work up your fingers.
Oh, yes.
Didn't that bother you?

I'll tell you about that. But I got the teacher, it was a German teacher there, in Omaha, Nebraska. So I took two lessons. What I wanted to learn how to do was slap the bass, (singing) one of those things, like --
I know, like [Braud] used to do.
Yeah, yeah.
Yeah.

He would say, 'You don't want to learn to slap a bass, you want to learn how to play the bass.' So I said, 'Okay.' So I took the two lessons. And I had to leave town. And the first thing they threw on me was 'White Heat.' And that was a fast number.
I remember Lunceford.
Right.
Yeah.
You know how fast that was.
Yeah.
And then it had that bass solo in there.
Yes, that's right.
My fingers was bleeding. I had blisters on them, and so I had to wrap my fingers in tape and all
like that. That's really awful, isn't it?
That was so bad.
Yeah. So -- yeah, because you just started right in to play bass. You hadn't worked up to it or you hadn't got the proper callouses.
That's right.
How long did it take you to where you could get out of pain?
Well, after I put the tape on, I noticed I could -- I didn't feel it so bad.
Yeah.
And so I just kept using the tape.
Yeah, until you got your fingers --
And started taking it off and started playing.
Yeah. Did you enjoy it?
Yes, I enjoyed it. I like bass, but --
But you didn't get enough rhythm out of it. You didn't get enough variety, horizon.
No, I really didn't learn to play it like I should, because I was cuffing my notes, as they said, where you use the whole hand instead of using your fingers.
Oh, I see.
But I would hit the right notes, each
time I played.
Yeah.
I would know how to read.
You'd use your wrist to get to it instead of your fingers.
Instead of my fingers, and I would slide up and down.
Yeah.
Even Ramey plays that way now sometimes.
Does he? Yeah.
One of those things.
Yeah, yeah.
